data.one_liner: A community-maintained collection of Dart lint rules for static analysis.
data.what_it_does: It bundles a large set of linter rules that can be included in a project’s analysis_options.yaml to enforce coding standards and catch potential bugs early. The rules are automatically updated and cover many common lint categories.
use_when: You want a ready-to-use, up-to-date set of lint rules for a Dart or Flutter project.
You need to enforce consistent code style and catch subtle bugs during development.
You prefer a single package to manage all lint rules instead of adding many individual packages.
avoid_when: You have a very small project and only need a few specific lints.
You already use a custom lint set that conflicts with the rules in this package.
You want to keep the analysis_options.yaml minimal and avoid a large number of rules.
strengths: Comprehensive coverage of many lint rules
Community updates keep the rules current
Easy to add via dev_dependencies and include in analysis_options.yaml
weaknesses: Large rule set may be overkill for small projects
Potential conflicts with other lint packages
No code generation or runtime features
data.setup_notes: Add to dev_dependencies and include package:all_lint_rules_community/all.yaml in analysis_options.yaml

alternatives.name: lints
alternatives.why_pick_it: Official linter package with a curated set of rules, often used as a base for Flutter projects

alternatives.name: flutter_lints
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a set of lint rules tailored for Flutter apps

data.minimal_example:
```yaml
# pubspec.yaml
dev_dependencies:
  all_lint_rules_community: ^0.0.43
```
```yaml
# analysis_options.yaml
include: package:all_lint_rules_community/all.yaml
```
